question: Should Telegram expose standalone `pin` and `unpin` message-tool actions, and what gate plus target semantics should protect persistent pinned-message mutations?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the feature would give agents bot-token-powered control over persistent chat pinned state, and current code has no pin-specific gate or approved implicit-unpin contract.

options.title: Approve gated explicit actions
options.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit action gate, require a concrete message id unless maintainers approve an implicit mode, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep delivery pin only
options.body: Do not expose standalone pin/unpin actions yet; keep current delivery pinning for messages OpenClaw just sent and document that boundary.

options.title: Request a design note first
options.body: Ask for a short design covering admin-right expectations, per-account gating, implicit unpin behavior, forum-topic semantics, and live proof before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve gated explicit actions
recommendation.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit action gate, require a concrete message id unless maintainers approve an implicit mode, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision extends the Telegram message-tool discovery and action-runtime seams gumadeiras consolidated.
